conventions.convention: The prescribed background is Minkowski spacetime with signature (-,+,+,+), length coordinate x⁰=ct, physical time t, reference velocity u₀=(1,0,0,0), and reference bulk pressure Π₀=0.

The adiabatic sector has δσ_p=0; r=δε and Π̂=δΠ have units Pa, w consists of the dimensionless spatial velocity variations, and a_s=e_vv/(n₀h₀)>0 is dimensionless. Bulk viscosity ζ₀ and relaxation time τ₀ have units Pa s and s.

The two effective linear systems are stipulated model inputs. First-variation families need not solve nonlinear equations away from the reference state; no nonlinear error estimate, lifespan, curved-background existence theorem or empirical applicability is asserted.

Both response theorems assume Countable Choice and use componentwise real Schwartz data on ℝ³ or smooth periodic data on T³_L, L>0. Fourier transforms use the negative-sign 2π normalization; contraction is asserted for t≥0 and every Sobolev exponent q≥0.

Causality allows equality: the perfect branch requires 0<a_s≤1, while the bulk branch requires positive coefficients and a_s+ζ₀/(τ₀h₀)≤1. Stability means energy and weighted Sobolev contraction, not decay of every mode.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts the perfect system r_t+c h₀ div w=0, w_t+(c a_s/h₀)∇r=0, and the bulk system r_t+c h₀ div w=0, w_t+(c/h₀)∇(a_s r+Π̂)=0, τ₀Π̂_t+Π̂=−ζ₀c div w, with the stated reference-state, positivity, regularity and unit conventions.

Under the stipulated perfect branch, c,h₀>0, 0<a_s≤1 and Countable Choice, every real Schwartz or smooth periodic initial datum has a unique global smooth solution with the stated conserved energy identity, nonincreasing weighted Sobolev norms for t≥0, characteristic speeds 0 and ±c√a_s, and shrinking-ball finite propagation at c√a_s≤c.

Under the stipulated bulk branch, h₀,T₀,c,a_s,ζ₀,τ₀>0, Countable Choice and a_s+ζ₀/(τ₀h₀)≤1, every real Schwartz or smooth periodic initial datum has a unique global smooth solution with the stated positive energy and dissipation identity, weighted Sobolev contraction for t≥0, and finite propagation at c√(a_s+ζ₀/(τ₀h₀))≤c. Energy contraction does not assert decay of every mode.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact sequence-indexed choice assumption explicitly carried by both response theorems and the example.
The mathematical evolution suppliers use its scalar Schwartz definition componentwise on real vector data; the assigned postulate states the matching definition.
The constant-coefficient evolution supplier transforms Schwartz data and uses the derivative and polynomial-multiplication identities under Countable Choice.
The evolution supplier reconstructs its global smooth solution by absolutely convergent inverse Fourier integrals.
The evolution supplier identifies Fourier energy with the corresponding L² framework under Countable Choice.
The evolution supplier identifies integral and Plancherel transforms as tempered distributions with the same negative-sign 2π normalization.
The evolution supplier's shrinking-ball energy proof applies outward-normal divergence integration on bounded smooth Euclidean balls.
Earlier material and geometric suppliers fix signature, future direction and smooth Lorentzian background conventions.
Earlier stress-projection suppliers use metric compatibility and tensor product/contraction rules; the prescribed Minkowski specialization has ordinary coordinate derivatives.
The local Gibbs supplier differentiates the state functions and obtains the fixed-entropy pressure-energy response used in the assigned postulate.

alerts.finding: Its sources.references entry calls arXiv:0906.4787v2 “Paul Romatschke, New Developments in Relativistic Viscous Hydrodynamics”. The opened author submission record identifies this exact arXiv ID and version as “Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy”: [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.4787). The reference title therefore does not match its linked source.
